propositions: When an ephemeral runner's final push is rejected after the Jira rebar-id label is written but before the local CREATE event and binding are durably published, the local state is lost while the Jira label persists, creating an unbound_jira drift.

The existing L10 guard in binding_walk skips adopt when a rebar-id label is present, and binding recovery only walks pending store entries, so the permanently stuck drift cannot be healed by any automated path.

Recovery extension in binding_walk phase-1b detects a marked-but-unstored key (deterministic inbound id label present, no binding-store entry, no local ticket) and replays the adopt through the existing inbound-create leaf instead of standing down.
The idempotent-replay recovery is keyed on the deterministic local id (_jira_key_to_local_id) so replayed adopt converges on the same local id, binding, and label without duplication.
Foreign/ghost markers, multi-marker keys, keys with existing store entries, and retired keys continue to stand down unconditionally, preserving existing L10/L11 protections.
bridge_fsck unbound_jira audit remains untouched and continues alerting on this class until the binding is restored.
